lines.text: [Verse 1 – Brian alone]
You learned to listen for the trouble
Hiding underneath a voice,
Find the fact inside the panic,
Help somebody make a choice.
Then you leave the midnight console,
Put the working world away,
Raise a harp against your breathing
And make sorrow find a name.
The fat, nerdy non-Mormon kid
In a Salt Lake certainty
Learned to stand outside the answers
And ask what truth requires to be.
Now you trust what can be witnessed,
What survives the measured test.
You keep one hand on the evidence
And somehow see the best.
[Pre-Chorus – Brian lead; Sean sustained harmony only]
You never dressed the moment up
Or reached for something clever.
You looked at me as though reporting
What you’d plainly observed.
[Chorus – Brian sings every line; Sean only echoes the title and sustains harmony]
You said, “You radiate love.”
[Sean: You radiate love]
Three words, quiet and clear—
Not something I had earned from you,
Not something I could lose through fear.
You didn’t only say you loved me.
You named what traveled out of me.
You held a mirror to a light
I’d been much too close to see.
Of all the words a friend could give,
The truest were enough:
You radiate love.
[Verse 2 – Brian solo vocal; harmonica answers after completed phrases]
You ask what can be duplicated.
I ask who lit the first event.
You say the claim requires a method.
I ask what all this wonder meant.
You want the cosmos under controls.
I want the cosmos running free.
You say, “Produce another supernova.”
I say, “Poor repeatability.”
You keep me honest with the numbers.
I keep kicking at the frame.
You make me show where I found knowledge.
I ask who gave the facts their names.
Somewhere between proof and wonder,
Between the solid and unseen,
Two stubborn men keep moving closer
To what either one might mean.
[Pre-Chorus – Sean harmony grows]
Maybe truth is more than either
Of our favorite ways to look.
Maybe every honest friendship
Leaves some margin in the book.
[Chorus – fuller duet harmony]
You said, “You radiate love.”
[Sean: You radiate love]
Three words, quiet and clear—
Not something I had earned from you,
Not something I could lose through fear.
You didn’t only say you loved me.
You named what traveled out of me.
You held a mirror to a light
I’d been much too close to see.
Of all the words a friend could give,
The truest were enough:
You radiate love.
[Verse 3 – Brian lead; Sean sustained harmony only]
We were handed old instructions
For the ways that men should bond:
Stand together under gunfire,
Never ask what hurts beyond.
Trade affection for allegiance.
Call the silence being strong.
Turn our tenderness to weapons
And prove the whole thing wrong.
But we never needed battle
To discover we were brothers,
Never had to spill our blood
To earn the trust we gave each other.
We built this out of listening,
Out of laughter, doubt and grace;
Out of staying for the hard truth
Without making love lose face.
[Bridge – Sean steps forward as co-lead]
[Sean]
Bring me what is observable.
Show me what survives the test.
[Brian]
Bring me what first made you wonder.
Show me what the test has missed.
[Sean]
Truth is more than what we wish for.
[Brian]
Truth is more than what we know.
[Both]
If two men can stand between them,
There are places both can go.
No rulebook made us brothers.
No battlefield was won.
We simply kept on showing up
When showing up was love.
You said, “You radiate love.”
And something in me changed.
A lifetime of uncertain mirrors
Could not make those words untrue again.
You didn’t only say you loved me.
You said love had made me home—
That people standing near my fire
Felt a warmth I hadn’t known.
If I have ever been that light,
Some part reflects because
My greatest friend stood close enough
To tell me what I was:
You radiate love.
[Outro – shared lead, close harmony; harmonica answers]
Perhaps we never touch a thing.
Perhaps the space remains.
Perhaps we’re fields of opposition
Giving matter shape and name.
[Brian]
But I have felt your friendship, Sean.
No instrument is needed.
[Sean]
If love requires observation—
[Both]
Consider it repeated.
[Sean]
You radiate love.
[Brian]
So do you.
